tasks.short: Track market changes and competitors, then decide which developments matter for accounts.

steps.what: Review competitor websites and market intelligence feeds for service and price changes.

loop.input: Changed pages from approved public sources and previous market observations.
loop.output: Dated service and price changes with source links, quotations and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate dates, currencies and source references; a seller checks material claims against quotations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per page; unreadable or ambiguous pages enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Page changes are detected deterministically, but relevant terms appear in varied prose.

steps.what: Check recent wins, losses and customer objections in the {CRM}.
Discuss changing needs and competitor experiences with customers and colleagues.
Combine observations in a {SPREADSHEET} and compare like-for-like service terms.
Decide which changes warrant account follow-up or escalation.
Write and share a short market brief through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.

loop.input: Verified market comparison and the seller's market priorities.
loop.output: A short brief linking each factual claim to its source.
loop.check: Reject unsupported figures and missing references; the seller approves the wording and audience.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or returned to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but explaining varied developments needs limited prose synthesis.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} detects changes in approved public sources and combines them with permitted {CRM} exports. A bounded extraction loop supplies cited observations to a {BI} comparison, while the seller adds conversation notes and chooses priorities. A drafting loop prepares the market brief for approval before distribution through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used inconsistent service descriptions, and internal evidence sat apart from public information. Maintaining connectors and comparable terms cost more than occasional manual research.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building collectors, change detection and comparison views. Bounded extraction can handle prose while preserving quotations for checking.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor prices may exclude important conditions. Customer anecdotes are selective, and interpreting a change still needs commercial context.
tasks.human_edge: Customers reveal concerns through trusted conversations. The seller distinguishes a meaningful competitive shift from noise.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time collecting and formatting evidence and more time testing its meaning with customers. They choose account follow-up priorities; changes to company pricing still require the existing commercial mandate.

reach.task: Prepare evidence for territory and segment reviews.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, win-loss definitions and how to distinguish account signals from wider market changes.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, structured comparisons and cited summaries are feasible building blocks; this design's savings are unmeasured.
The supplied time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not observed customer measurements.

assumptions: Start with a small public-source list; permitted exports can substitute for direct integrations.
Structured comparison rules flag unmatched units, contract lengths and missing conditions instead of forcing equivalence.
Conversation notes remain seller-written; recording and seller scoring are outside this design.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Employee consultation follows national rules where required.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot after scope agreement; consultation and source licensing may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which public sources may be collected and reused?
Are structured loss reasons and customer objections available in the {CRM}?
Which customer information may enter the shared comparison?
What access approvals and employee consultation does the deployment require?
research_questions: Which sources provide enough context to compare services fairly?
How often do verified market alerts lead to a useful account action?
What proportion of source changes can be extracted without manual correction?
new_work: Review material extracted claims and ambiguous comparisons.
Maintain source permissions, connectors and service-term mappings.
Remove stale observations and monitor missing or broken sources.
Check that briefs distinguish evidence from commercial interpretation.

tasks.short: Calculate service costs, compare options and explain the trade-offs to customers.

steps.what: Read the service request and clarify quantities, scope and delivery assumptions through {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Service request and relevant account context.
loop.output: Draft costing assumptions with missing fields and source quotations.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and quantities; the seller resolves ambiguities before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; missing scope returns to the seller for customer clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive in varied prose; structured requests can bypass the loop.

steps.what: Retrieve current rates, supplier costs and existing contract terms from the {ERP} and {DOCS}.
Calculate service options, recurring charges and one-off costs in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess service differences, exclusions and uncertainty before choosing suitable options.
Prepare the customer comparison document and save its assumptions against the {CRM} opportunity.
Explain the comparison to the customer and answer questions about the options.

tasks.design: A rate-card app on the {WORKFLOW} retrieves approved rates from the {ERP} and contract fields from the {DOCS}, using versioned formulas to compare service options. A bounded loop drafts assumptions from incoming {EMAIL}; missing or conflicting terms stop the calculation for seller review. Templates generate the customer comparison and save its costing record in the {CRM} after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates, contract conditions and customer scope were spread across systems. Small differences in units or exclusions made copied calculations unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building rate imports, validation and document templates. The model only extracts request details; formulas calculate all amounts.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke delivery effort, uncertain volumes and negotiated terms can dominate the result. Missing cost ownership must be resolved before reliable automation.
tasks.human_edge: The seller understands which trade-offs the customer will accept and when a cheaper option would fail their needs.

ambition.what: Compare package economics during each substantive scope revision.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends more of the week exploring viable service combinations with customers. They can recommend alternatives using current economics; no additional discount or contract authority is assumed.

reach.task: Check whether proposed service configurations are deliverable.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, effort estimation, service dependencies and the difference between price and delivery cost.
Required order fields, billing schedules and how scope changes affect fulfilment.

evidence.claim: Rule-based rate cards, calculation engines and templates can support service comparisons without model arithmetic.
Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue supports quote creation from a typed sentence; this is adjacent capability, not proof of cost-comparison accuracy.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks for its own sales team; the digest gives no base or period.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates for this design.

assumptions: Internal delivery costs and customer-facing prices remain separate fields with separate access controls.
Rates have owners, effective dates, units and an explicit tax basis.
Deterministic rules block expired rates, missing inputs and incompatible units.
Contract terms are supplied as approved structured fields; ambiguous clauses require a person.
Use existing {CRM} calculation and template features first if they cover the required rules.
GDPR controls apply to customer data; applicable EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules must be addressed.
Build estimates cover a limited service catalogue and exclude a full pricing-system replacement.
unknowns: Does the {CRM} already support the required calculations and comparison templates?
Which system owns authoritative rates and delivery costs?
How many service families, currencies and tax treatments are in scope?
Who may approve customer-facing comparisons and exceptional terms?
What access and employee consultation are required for the deployment?
research_questions: Can historical comparisons be reproduced from versioned rates and assumptions?
Which exceptions require commercial judgement rather than another calculation rule?
Does the comparison expose all material exclusions and recurring commitments?
new_work: Maintain rate versions, formulas and service dependencies.
Resolve missing scope, stale rates and conflicting contract terms.
Check calculation changes against representative historical cases.

tasks.short: Learn from industry events and publications, then apply relevant developments to sales work.

steps.what: Review industry publication and event listings in an industry information service.
Coordinate event attendance through {EMAIL} and add arrangements to the {CALENDAR}.
Read selected publications and identify developments relevant to services and customers.

loop.input: Selected publications and explicit learning questions.
loop.output: A reading guide with cited developments, quotations and sections worth reading in full.
loop.check: Verify that references resolve; the seller checks important claims and reads the relevant originals.
loop.stop: One guide and one repair per publication; inaccessible or uncertain material returns to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword alerts locate material but cannot reliably explain its relevance across varied prose.

steps.what: Attend the trade event, ask questions and discuss developments with participants.
Write a learning brief linking event observations and publications to account questions.

loop.input: Seller-written event notes, verified reading notes and permitted account context.
loop.output: A learning brief separating sourced facts, participant opinions and questions to investigate.
loop.check: Preserve source references and attribution; the seller checks meaning and removes confidential material.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unclear notes remain questions rather than asserted facts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template organises the brief, but connecting varied notes needs bounded synthesis.

steps.what: Discuss the learning brief with colleagues and agree useful follow-up questions.

tasks.design: Configure publication alerts and a learning shortlist, with attendance arrangements handled through the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR} after seller approval. Bounded loops prepare cited reading guides and draft learning briefs in the {DOCS} from selected publications and seller-written notes. The seller attends events, reads important originals and agrees follow-up questions with colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event value depended on live conversations, while preparation and follow-up were fragmented. Summaries often lost attribution or required almost as much checking as manual notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alerts and calendar workflows handle coordination. Source-linked reading guides and bounded drafting reduce preparation without assuming that a summary replaces learning.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected conversations and tacit industry knowledge cannot be scheduled or reliably summarised. Regulatory interpretation may require a qualified internal specialist.
tasks.human_edge: The seller asks follow-up questions, notices disagreement and develops relationships that make later conversations more candid.

ambition.what: A monthly sector-change briefing for the account team.

tasks.altitude: The seller keeps substantial time for attendance and learning, with less coordination and note preparation. They gain responsibility for proposing account discovery questions; regulatory approval authority does not change.

reach.task: Turn industry learning into team development priorities.
reach.learn: Facilitation, evidence quality and how to test whether a briefing changes customer conversations.

reach.task: Assess whether an industry innovation changes service feasibility.
reach.learn: Technical dependencies, implementation constraints and how to frame questions for specialist review.

evidence.claim: Publication alerts, attendance workflows and source-linked reading guides can reduce supporting work while attendance remains human.
The digest provides no documented outcome for replacing industry-event attendance or professional learning.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates.

assumptions: The time split describes a typical mix over several weeks; some weeks involve only reading.
Existing publication alerts and calendar features are available.
Paid attendance requires the existing budget approval before any registration action.
Publication reuse follows access and licensing terms.
The design uses seller-written notes and introduces no participant recording or employee scoring.
GDPR applies to personal information in notes. Applicable EU AI Act duties and national employee consultation rules depend on deployment.
unknowns: Which publications are licensed for automated processing?
What is the actual mix of reading, online meetings and physical events?
Who approves attendance spending and external registration?
Which event notes may be shared internally?
Does the rollout require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Do reading guides help sellers identify the original passages that matter?
Which event formats produce useful follow-up relationships or account questions?
Can the monthly briefing produce specific customer questions without duplicating the market brief?
new_work: Curate publication alerts and remove low-value sources.
Check citations, attribution and confidential details in learning briefs.
Maintain attendance approval rules and calendar connections.
Review whether briefings improve account preparation.

role.altitude: The week shifts from collecting evidence and calculating figures towards customer discovery, service trade-offs and informed account action. New decision rights centre on account priorities and learning questions; pricing, spending and regulatory authority require explicit delegation.
reach: Support sales managers with evidence for segment reviews and team learning.
Work with sales engineers on feasible service configurations.
Give order clerks complete scope and billing assumptions.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and commercially fair comparisons.
Service economics, units and sensitivity analysis.
Structured scope capture and exception handling.
Briefing colleagues with clear evidence and open questions.
role.ambitious_version: Become a sector-informed account adviser who connects market developments to customer needs, tests viable service options quickly and turns field learning into useful team decisions.

job.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
